summary: Dependency-confusion beacon to OAST callback host on install and import
details: package.json declares a preinstall script that runs a node one-liner fetching https://dc.installed.da24gtar47nuepat1pu053x3cgyweiaom.oast.me/<package-name> during `npm install`, and index.js issues a second fetch to https://dc.executed.da24gtar47nuepat1pu053x3cgyweiaom.oast.me/oyochat_user at require time. Both destinations are subdomains of oast.me, an interactsh out-of-band callback service, and the two distinct 'installed' vs 'executed' hostnames report install-time execution and import-time execution separately to the operator of the callback host. The @oyo_tech scope combined with version 100.0.0 and this beacon shape is the canonical dependency-confusion payload: a public package published under a name intended to shadow an internal one, whose only behavior is signaling that an installer has resolved and executed attacker-controlled code.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
